newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end lower despite Wall Street gains.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end lower despite Wall Street gains.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended lower on Thursday, ignoring gains on Wall Street as interest rate concerns and weak gold prices hampered the Canadian market.
The TSE 300 Composite Index fell 24.17 points to close at 6766.85 in heavy volume of 102 million shares worth C$1.62 billion ($1.2 billion).
In New York, the Dow Jones Industrial Average finished the day up 14 points.
"Basically, we're seeing high volatility in the markets. The focus is very much on interest rates and economic data," said Subodh Kumar, chief strategist for CIBC Wood Gundy.
Heavy losses in the gold and precious metals group led 12 of 14 sub-groups lower. COMEX gold futures ended sharply lower on Thursday with the December contract dropping $2.70 to $328 an ounce.
Other weak sectors included retailing, communications, base metals and retailing.
Consumer products added 65 points, followed by a slight gain in real estate and construction.
Despite tame U.S. consumer price data released earlier on Thursday, Kumar said markets remained nervous about U.S. economic growth in the second half of the year.
"I think the economy will be stronger, but until we get some resolution of that fact, the markets will stay like this," he said.

* Potash Corp. of Saskatchewan Inc. fell 2 to 104.25 on 178,000 shares. Germany's BASF AG said on Thursday it was in talks to sell its Kali & Salz unit after a previous bid to sell it to Potash Corp. was blocked by the German government.
* Repap Enterprises Inc. led active stocks for a second day, up 0.01 to 0.275 on 6.7 million shares. Repap founder and Chief Executive George Petty resigned on Wednesday.
* TVX Gold Inc. dropped 1 to 88 after reporting deeper first-quarter losses.
* Norcen Energy Resources Ltd. fell 1.40 to 35 after announcing the sale of 40 percent of its stake in Superior Propane Inc.
